references.text: Abraham asks his servant to swear by placing his hand under his thigh, a similar oath-taking act as when Jacob asked Joseph to swear to bury him in Canaan.
The servant places his hand under Abraham's thigh and swears, paralleling how Joseph swore to Jacob.
Joseph asks Pharaoh for permission to fulfill the oath he swore to his father Jacob to bury him in Canaan.
King David bowed on his bed in worship, a parallel to Israel bowing at the head of the bed.
The book of Hebrews quotes this event: By faith Jacob, when dying, blessed each son and bowed over the top of his staff (the head of the bed in the Hebrew text).
Both verses illustrate Jacob's use of an oath as a legally binding means to secure God's promises regarding inheritance and the future.
Both verses show how an oath sworn by the Lord is used to ensure that God's promises concerning inheritance (throne or land) are fulfilled.
